title: Sorted segment with preserved cells
statement: For functions $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, natural numbers $a,fr$, and a list $L$ of integers, the property holds when both of the following are true: there is a list $L'$ occupying the segment specified by $\mu'$ starting at $a$, such that $L'$ is a permutation of $L$ and is nondecreasing; and the memory specified by $\mu'$ is obtained from $\mu$ by preserving the required cells outside that segment for a length of $L$.
caveat: The supplied material does not define the segment predicate or the memory-preservation predicate, so their exact meanings cannot be stated more precisely.
